ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a cubic cake divided by grid lines into small cubes; the visible top face, front face, and side face each have every edge divided into 4 segments, so it corresponds to a 4×4×4 cube, with a total of 64 1×1×1 small cubes. Reasoning: The problem states that only the top face and the four vertical side faces have icing, and the bottom face does not have icing. For a small cube to have exactly two faces with icing, it must be located on the intersection line of exactly two outer surfaces that have icing. Classification counting: 1. Small cubes on the four edges of the top face but not at the vertices: each top edge has 4 small cubes; removing the two vertices leaves 4−2=2; altogether 4×2=8. These small cubes touch the top face and one side face, so exactly two faces have icing. 2. Small cubes on the four vertical edges where two side faces intersect: each vertical edge has 4 small cubes. The topmost one also touches the top face, so it has 3 faces with icing and must be excluded; the remaining 3 touch only two side faces, and even if the bottom face is at the lowest layer, it has no icing, so they still have exactly two faces with icing. Altogether 4×3=12. The total is 8+12=20.

method.method_draft: Use an edge-classification count. First read the image as a cube subdivided into a 4-by-4 grid on each visible face, confirming there are 4 small cubes along every edge. From the text, note that only the top face and the four vertical side faces are iced; the bottom face is not iced. A small cube has exactly two iced sides only when it lies on the intersection of exactly two iced exterior faces. Count two types: (a) cubes on the four top edges but not at the top corners, giving 4 edges × (4−2) = 8; (b) cubes on the four vertical edges where two side faces meet, excluding the top corner cube on each vertical edge because it also has top icing, giving 4 edges × 3 = 12. Add 8 + 12 = 20.
